title: Evaluation-defined scalar Hom maps respect coefficient towers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $R\xrightarrow{a}S\xrightarrow{b}V$ be homomorphisms of sheaves of commutative rings. Use the ordinary unbounded derived module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], their closed tensor and internal-Hom structures [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], and derived scalar extensions $T_a,T_b,T_{ba}$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Equip them with the canonical tensor comparisons $\mu_a:T_a(P\otimes^LQ)\cong T_aP\otimes^LT_aQ$ and balanced scalar associator $\alpha:T_bT_a\cong T_{ba}$, normalized on K-flat representatives. Assume the tensor-tower and identity equations of [lem-sfb-scalar-hom-tensor-coherence] for these comparisons. Write $H_R,H_S,H_V$ for the derived internal Homs [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], with evaluation in the convention $P\otimes H_R(P,Q)\to Q$ (using symmetry when needed). Define
$$c^a_{P,Q}:T_aH_R(P,Q)\longrightarrow H_S(T_aP,T_aQ)$$
to be the transpose of $T_aP\otimes T_aH_R(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\mu_a^{-1}}T_a(P\otimes H_R(P,Q))\xrightarrow{T_a(\operatorname{ev})}T_aQ$, and define $c^b,c^{ba}$ likewise. These maps are natural contravariantly in $P$ and covariantly in $Q$, and satisfy
$$H_V(\alpha_P^{-1},\alpha_Q)\,c^b_{T_aP,T_aQ}\,T_b(c^a_{P,Q})=c^{ba}_{P,Q}\,\alpha_{H_R(P,Q)}.$$
For the identity ring map, $c^{\mathrm{id}}$ is the identity under the scalar multiplication unitor. No flatness, finite-freeness, perfectness, boundedness or completeness assumption is required; the assertion concerns these maps, not their invertibility.

proof.text: For each coefficient ring $W$, use the natural closed adjunction already supplied in M.closed by [def-sfb-scalar-hom-comparison-data]. Composing its tensor argument with the specified symmetry gives the convention in the statement: $\operatorname{Hom}(X,H_W(P,Q))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes X,Q)$. Write $e^W_{P,Q}:P\otimes H_W(P,Q)\to Q$. The inverse bijection sends $h$ to $e^W_{P,Q}(1_P\otimes h)$, so it is injective. Naturality of this bijection gives $e^W_{P',Q'}(1\otimes H_W(f,g))=g\,e^W_{P,Q}(f\otimes1)$ for $f:P'\to P$ and $g:Q\to Q'$. Throughout, juxtaposition denotes composition with the rightmost map applied first; tensors are derived over the current coefficient ring.

proof.text: Put $t^a_{P,X}=\mu_a(P,X)^{-1}$. By the defining transpose, $c^a_{P,Q}$ is the unique arrow with $e^S_{T_aP,T_aQ}(1\otimes c^a_{P,Q})=T_a(e^R_{P,Q})t^a_{P,H_R(P,Q)}$. The same equation holds for $b$ and $ba$. This is just application of the bijection of Step 1 to the composite in the statement; it imposes no invertibility condition on $c^a$. proof.text:
We check both variables at once. Write $F=T_a$, $H=H_R(P,Q)$, $H'=H_R(P',Q')$ and $h=H_R(f,g)$, where $f:P'\to P$, $g:Q\to Q'$. The uncurried map of $H_S(Ff,Fg)c^a_{P,Q}$, relative to $FP'$, is
$$Fg\,F(e^R_{P,Q})t^a_{P,H}(Ff\otimes1)=F\bigl(g\,e^R_{P,Q}(f\otimes1)\bigr)t^a_{P',H}=F(e^R_{P',Q'})t^a_{P',H'}(1\otimes Fh).$$
The first equality is naturality of $t^a$ in $P$; the second is the evaluation identity of Step 1 and naturality of $t^a$ in $H$. The last expression is the uncurry of $c^a_{P',Q'}Fh$ by Step 2. Injectivity in Step 1 proves naturality, with exactly the asserted variance. Replace $a$ by $b$ or $ba$ for the other two maps. The private scalarEvaluation_naturality and scalarBaseChangeHom_naturality prove this directly from the closed-structure fields, without an existence theorem.

proof.text:
Write $F=T_a$, $G=T_b$, $K=GF$, $J=T_{ba}$, $H=H_R(P,Q)$ and $d=c^b_{FP,FQ}\,G(c^a_{P,Q})$. Its uncurry relative to $KP$ is
$$e^V_{KP,KQ}(1\otimes d)=G(e^S_{FP,FQ})t^b_{FP,H_S(FP,FQ)}(1\otimes Gc^a_{P,Q})=G\bigl(e^S_{FP,FQ}(1\otimes c^a_{P,Q})\bigr)t^b_{FP,FH}=K(e^R_{P,Q})G(t^a_{P,H})t^b_{FP,FH}.$$
Here Step 2 for $b$ gives the first equality, naturality of $t^b$ gives the second, and Step 2 for $a$ gives the third. Define $t^K_{P,X}=G(t^a_{P,X})t^b_{FP,FX}$. Thus the uncurried map is explicitly $K(e^R_{P,Q})t^K_{P,H}$.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (sites-cohomology-lemma-internal-hom), equation-internal-hom; Tag 07A4 (sites-cohomology-lemma-pullback-tensor-product). Formal evaluation-transpose calculation by the worker, not a tower theorem stated in Stacks.

proof.text:
Use the hypothesis htower for the supplied comparisons; no application of a tensor-coherence existence theorem is required. In the notation of Step 4 it reads $(\alpha_P\otimes\alpha_X)\mu_b(FP,FX)G(\mu_a(P,X))=\mu_{ba}(P,X)\alpha_{P\otimes X}$. Composing with inverses of the tensor comparisons gives the useful form
$$\alpha_{P\otimes X}t^K_{P,X}=t^{ba}_{P,X}(\alpha_P\otimes\alpha_X).$$
This rearrangement only cancels the specified isomorphisms. In particular, precomposing at $X=H$ by $\alpha_P^{-1}\otimes1_{KH}$ yields $\alpha_{P\otimes H}t^K_{P,H}(\alpha_P^{-1}\otimes1)=t^{ba}_{P,H}(1_{JP}\otimes\alpha_H)$.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (sites-cohomology-lemma-internal-hom), equation-internal-hom; Tag 07A4 (sites-cohomology-lemma-pullback-tensor-product). Formal evaluation-transpose calculation by the worker, not a tower theorem stated in Stacks.

proof.text:
We now uncurry the two arrows in the asserted tower equation relative to $JP$. By naturality of evaluation (Step 1), the left side uncurries to $\alpha_Q e^V_{KP,KQ}(\alpha_P^{-1}\otimes d)$. Substituting Step 4, naturality of $\alpha$ at $e^R_{P,Q}$, and then Step 5 gives the full calculation
$$\alpha_Q K(e^R_{P,Q})t^K_{P,H}(\alpha_P^{-1}\otimes1)=J(e^R_{P,Q})\alpha_{P\otimes H}t^K_{P,H}(\alpha_P^{-1}\otimes1)=J(e^R_{P,Q})t^{ba}_{P,H}(1\otimes\alpha_H).$$
By Step 2 this last map is $e^V_{JP,JQ}(1\otimes c^{ba}_{P,Q}\alpha_H)$, the uncurry of the right side. Injectivity in Step 1 proves precisely $H_V(\alpha_P^{-1},\alpha_Q)d=c^{ba}_{P,Q}\alpha_H$. Both sides have source $KH$ and target $H_V(JP,JQ)$. The private scalarBaseChangeHom_tower performs this calculation in arbitrary categories and is specialized to the scalar functors.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (sites-cohomology-lemma-internal-hom), equation-internal-hom; Tag 07A4 (sites-cohomology-lemma-pullback-tensor-product). Formal evaluation-transpose calculation by the worker, not a tower theorem stated in Stacks.

proof.text:
For the identity ring map put $I=T_{\mathrm{id}}$ and let $u:I\cong\mathrm{Id}$ be the scalar multiplication unitor. The identity equation supplied as the hypothesis hid is $u_P^{-1}\otimes u_X^{-1}=\mu_{\mathrm{id}}(P,X)u_{P\otimes X}^{-1}$. Cancel its isomorphisms to get $u_{P\otimes X}t^{\mathrm{id}}_{P,X}=u_P\otimes u_X$. With $H=H_R(P,Q)$, the uncurry relative to $P$ of the transported comparison $H_R(u_P^{-1},u_Q)c^{\mathrm{id}}_{P,Q}$ is therefore
$$u_Q I(e^R_{P,Q})t^{\mathrm{id}}_{P,H}(u_P^{-1}\otimes1)=e^R_{P,Q}u_{P\otimes H}t^{\mathrm{id}}_{P,H}(u_P^{-1}\otimes1)=e^R_{P,Q}(1\otimes u_H).$$
The first equality is naturality of $u$, the second the just displayed tensor equation. The uncurried maps of the transported comparison and $u_H$ agree, so Step 1 gives $H_R(u_P^{-1},u_Q)c^{\mathrm{id}}_{P,Q}=u_H$. Identifying $IH$ with $H$ by $u_H$ makes this exactly the identity claimed. The private scalarBaseChangeHom_identity proves this by uncurry injectivity and cancellation of the tensor image of the unitor isomorphisms.
